limits: Only fixed fixture records, methods, models and palette storage are qualified. Arbitrary live model/material/resource ownership, native exceptions and whole scene/Present remain open.

The twenty refusal cases mutate a copied real frame and restored fixture fields to test the predicate; they are not twenty whole native fallback executions. External callback fallback additionally runs through the native loop and compares twelve pairs per process.

The captured path preserves native group prepare/finish and reference counts, and folds plugin mesh-event statistics with the existing aggregate helper. It does not retain per-mesh timing intervals when there is no external callback.
Begin flags=7 and deferred driver-error limitations from the command experiment remain. No gameplay FPS estimate or multiplayer proof follows.
Profiling is diagnostic wall time under contention. Four-way uninstrumented rotations compare native bulk, direct bulk capture, worker bulk capture and the prior per-mesh worker.
The native baseline goes through an additional flag-preserving mode dispatch at the fixture hook. Production code is unchanged.

Each frame still performs synchronous ownership and frame-start handoffs, then waits for full GPU completion. These fixture barriers may hide useful overlap, but cannot simply be omitted from reported cost.
audit_refinement: Native D3D9 AddRef during D3DX texture assignment is a device-lifetime call. Permit and count only IUnknown AddRef/Release inside explicit source-assignment or queued-resource ownership scopes; all state calls, state-block calls and unscoped lifetime calls still fail. A new unscoped AddRef fault proves the boundary.
next_boundary: First compare including the leader in the checked instanced submission: the current consumer issues an ordinary leader plus two follower batches (three draws for 25 units), while native bulk uses two. Then test redundant ownership/frame-start barriers, retaining complete timings and ownership/failure controls.
